entities.summary:
Saint Breage, a revered figure within the traditions of early Insular Christianity, is a legendary Irish missionary saint believed to have journeyed from Ireland to Cornwall, England, during the 5th or 6th century CE. While concrete biographical details and exact dates are scarce, typical of many early Celtic saints, her significance lies in her traditional role in the Christianization of Cornwall and the enduring local veneration that led to the naming of a parish and church in her honor. Her story is intertwined with the broader movement of Irish monasticism and missionary zeal, known as *peregrinatio pro Christo*, which saw numerous saints establish new Christian communities across Britain and Europe.

According to hagiographical accounts, Breage embarked on a voyage from Ireland, possibly alongside other saints such as Germoe and Sennen, landing on the southern coast of Cornwall. She is said to have established a religious settlement or hermitage in the area now known as Breage, near Helston. Her mission involved converting the local populace, often depicted as challenging the existing pagan or Celtic spiritual practices. Though specific miracles or detailed narratives of her ministry are sparse, her presence signifies the transmission of Christian faith, monastic practices, and cultural influence from the flourishing Christian centers of Ireland to the southwestern tip of Britain during the post-Roman period.
